record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.original_question: Develop a theory of geometric conditions that define or characterize strata for tensegrities in multidimensional Euclidean spaces, beyond the planar case.

evidence.quote: There is almost nothing known in multidimensional case. Problem 9 Develop theory of geometric conditions for strata in multidimensional case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V=\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$, and fix an integer $d\ge 2$. A configuration of $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a map $P:V\to\mathbb{R}^d$, $v_i\mapsto p_i$; the configuration space is identified with $(\mathbb{R}^d)^n$. A self-stress on $(G,P)$ is an assignment of weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}\in\mathbb{R}$ to each edge $\{v_i,v_j\}\in E$ satisfying the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j:\{v_i,v_j\}\in E} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0\qquad\text{for every } i=1,\dots,n.$$
A tensegrity supported on $G$ is a pair $(P,w)$ where $w$ is a nonzero self-stress. The set
$$W(G)=\{P\in(\mathbb{R}^d)^n : (G,P)\text{ admits a nonzero self-stress}\}$$
is naturally stratified according to the dimension of the space of self-stresses; its strata $W_k(G)=\{P:\dim\ker=k\}$ partition the configuration space.

In the planar case $d=2$, each stratum can be characterized by explicit geometric incidence conditions on the points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ (for example, classical conditions such as "six points lie on a conic" arising via Cayley-type meet-join expressions in the projective plane).

Problem: For arbitrary $d\ge 3$, develop a theory of geometric (incidence-type) conditions on configurations $P=(p_1,\dots,p_n)\in(\mathbb{R}^d)^n$ that define and characterize the strata $W_k(G)$ of the configuration space of tensegrities supported on $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. In particular, produce a system of geometric conditions, expressed via projective incidence operations among the points and the linear subspaces they span, that is necessary and sufficient for a generic configuration to admit a nonzero self-stress with prescribed combinatorial type, generalizing the known planar characterization to all higher dimensions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing strata of tensegrity configuration spaces by geometric conditions has been resolved in the planar case via Cayley/meet-join incidence conditions, but in dimensions d ≥ 3 essentially nothing is known. Recent literature on stresses in frameworks (e.g., the combinatorial geometry of stresses) addresses related questions but does not provide a general theory of geometric conditions for strata in higher dimensions, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
status_evidence.snippet: There is almost nothing known in the multidimensional case.
status_evidence.claim: The multidimensional theory of geometric conditions for strata of tensegrity configuration spaces is essentially undeveloped.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric conditions characterize strata of plane tensegrities via meet-join (Cayley) operations.
status_evidence.claim: The planar case is well understood, providing the baseline that higher-dimensional generalizations seek to extend.

status_evidence.title: The combinatorial geometry of stresses in frameworks
status_evidence.snippet: Studies stresses in frameworks combinatorially but does not yield a complete stratification theory in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work on stresses in frameworks has not produced a general higher-dimensional theory of strata-defining geometric conditions.
